subject.title: Windows QuickStart defaults first chat to paid Anthropic model without credit warning

question: What should Windows QuickStart do when a first-run Anthropic selection resolves to the paid Opus default before the first Terminal chat?
rationale: Changing the default model, adding a blocking billing preflight, or relying on post-failure copy affects provider policy, onboarding UX, and existing model-selection expectations.

options.title: Warn before hatch
options.body: Keep explicit Anthropic selection, but show a clear paid-credit warning or confirmation plus a switch-provider/model path before the first Terminal chat.

options.title: Change first-run default
options.body: Choose a cheaper maintainer-approved Anthropic or beta/tester model for fresh QuickStart setups when available, while preserving existing configured models.

options.title: Document intentional paid default
options.body: Leave Opus as the first-run default and rely on improved billing error copy plus docs, accepting the onboarding friction.

recommendation.title: Warn before hatch
recommendation.body: Keep explicit Anthropic selection, but show a clear paid-credit warning or confirmation plus a switch-provider/model path before the first Terminal chat.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history points to steipete on the Anthropic default policy and current setup path carry-forward.
